title: Kiara Advani's Co-Star Calls Out Gender Bias After Toxic Song Backlash
excerpt: British actor Benedict Garrett defended Advani against online trolls who attacked her for intimate scenes with Yash in the 'Tabaahi' music video, asking why only the woman faces abuse when both actors are married with children.
body:
• Benedict Garrett, Kiara Advani's co-star in the upcoming film Toxic, publicly called out the gender double standard in how audiences reacted to the 'Tabaahi' song's intimate sequences.
  • While Yash received praise and 'fire emojis' for the same scenes, Advani was trolled with comments questioning her choices as a married woman and mother.
  • Advani had earlier dismissed reports that she asked makers to tone down intimate scenes with Yash, calling them 'absolute nonsense.'
  • Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups, directed by Geetu Mohandas, is scheduled for release on August 26, 2026.

The release of the Tabaahi music video from the upcoming film Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups was supposed to build buzz for one of Bollywood's most anticipated releases of the year. Instead, it triggered a wave of online abuse directed squarely at Kiara Advani — while her male co-star Yash drew nothing but praise for the exact same scenes.

British actor Benedict Garrett, who also stars in Toxic, broke his silence with an Instagram video that laid bare the disparity.

"I've seen people praising Yash, filling his comments with fire emojis and saying how amazing he looks. But when it comes to Kiara Advani, she's become the butt of jokes. People are saying things like, oh, she only just got married, she's a mother, she's on a honeymoon instead of Sidharth Malhotra. Seriously?"

— Benedict Garrett, actor in Toxic

The Double Standard

The backlash against Advani centered on her personal life. Trolls flooded her Instagram comments with attacks that framed her intimate scenes with Yash as a betrayal of her husband, Sidharth Malhotra, and inappropriate for a mother — Advani and Malhotra have a young daughter, Saraayah.

Garrett pointed out that the same logic should apply to Yash, who is married to actress Radhika Pandit and has two children. Yet Yash's comment sections were filled exclusively with praise.

"Yash is also married, he also has children. So why is only the woman getting the abuse, while the man apparently gets the applause?" Garrett said. "They are actors. Their job is to act, to portray characters, to make you believe that they are in love, even when they're not. Their job is to tell stories that reflect the human experience."

Advani's Response

Advani had already addressed related speculation in May, when reports emerged claiming she asked the makers to trim intimate scenes after watching the final cut. She posted a screenshot of the report on her Instagram story with two words: "Absolute nonsense."

In a later interview with Bombay Times, Advani spoke more expansively about the film's exploration of relationships. "With Toxic, I think it completely changes the way you see the man-woman dynamic," she said. "Even for me, when Geetu narrated the script, it took a while to understand that okay, this is also normal. It may be grey, it may be not in your conventional space, but there's a certain liberation in love."

About the Film

Directed by Geetu Mohandas — an award-winning filmmaker and founding member of the Women in Cinema Collective — Toxic is an action thriller filmed simultaneously in Kannada and English. It features an ensemble cast including Nayanthara, Huma Qureshi, Tara Sutaria, and Rukmini Vasanth, with music by Ravi Basrur and action choreography by JJ Perry and Anbariv.

The film is set for release on August 26, 2026, after multiple postponements from earlier dates. It will be released in dubbed versions across Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, and other languages.

The controversy has sparked renewed debate about whether Indian audiences hold female performers to a fundamentally different standard than their male counterparts — a conversation that cuts across both the domestic industry and its massive global diaspora audience.
nri_angle: The controversy reflects broader conversations about gender double standards in Indian entertainment that resonate with diaspora audiences following Bollywood from abroad.
